newsitem.title: USA: Pool drain covers recalled after two drownings.
newsitem.headline: Pool drain covers recalled after two drownings.

text.p: About 206,000 pool drain covers for spas, hot tubs and swimming pools are being recalled after two drownings were linked to the covers, the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission said Monday.

The drain covers, made by Hydro-Air Industries of Orange, Calif., are meant to cover pipes carrying water out of pools and tubs. But under some circumstances, a bather's head can be held underwater if the bather's hair becomes entangled in the cover, the commission said in a statement.
Hydro-Air is aware of two drownings and one near-drowning resulting from hair getting trapped in the drain cover, model 10-6200, the statement said.
The drain cover is a white circular plastic disc installed in spas, hot tubs and pools from 1980 to 1995.
Consumers who have this model should immediately stop using their spas, hot tubs and swimming pools and contact Hydro-Air at 800-230 9560 to receive a free replacement part.
